title: Awareness and metacognitive reports share mechanisms

statements.text: The joint statement of the higher-order approach by Brown, Lau and LeDoux, as cited by Fleming, holds that conscious awareness and metacognitive reports depend on shared mechanisms in the human brain, and higher-order inference may run without strategic cognitive access such as working memory.
statements.scope: Cited through Fleming 2020. The Brown, Lau and LeDoux paper is not among the sources read.

sources.quote: A stronger reading of the model is that conscious awareness and metacognitive reports depend on shared mechanisms in the human brain
making it compatible with higher-order representational accounts of phenomenal consciousness
